Of course, more problems will be encountered in spreading that impact of recovery over a wide part of the animal's original range.

But there are fewer natural limitations to the potential. Restoration of the three prairie chickens to one or two areas in all States within their former ranges is conceivable. The impact on the species as well as other associated grassland species would be considerable.
Economic impact: The discussion of the economic impact of endangered species management and restoration is a reflection of the economic consequences of an effective program. Such consequences are considered not only at the national level but at the local and international levels as well. Impacts to the economy are considered to be of three types: (1) a direct impact, either positive or negative, based on the value of the endangered animal or its products; (2) an indirect impact based on the cost of foregoing, postponing, or in any way altering the use of resources found to be in conflict with the welfare of an endangered species; and (3) an indirect impact based on the increase in value of resources enhance or created by the recovery program for an endangered species.
